keywords: story of king shahryar and his brother
full_text:
King Shahryar, ruler of Persia and India, discovers his wife's mistrust and banishes her. Embittered, he grew mistrustful of everyone in his court until Shahrazad arrived. His brother Shahzaman had similar fate.

Vizier's daughter Shahrazad, learned in books and stories, volunteers to marry the king, with plan to tell stories and teach him compassion and wisdom through tales. With her sister Dunyazad, she begins tales that last 1001 nights, each ending on cliffhanger.

full_text:
A merchant stops to eat dates and throws pits, accidentally killing a Jinni's son. Jinni appears demanding death. Merchant begs leave to settle affairs and returns.

On his way, he meets three old Shaykhs each with an animal. They bargain with Jinni by telling wondrous tales, each tale buying one-third of merchant's blood. After three stories, Jinni forgives merchant.

title: The Fisherman and the Jinni (ಕನ್ನಡ)
summary: A poor fisherman casts net four times. Fourth time he pulls brass jar sealed with Solomon's seal. Opens it, huge Jinni emerges, threatens to kill fisherman because after centuries imprisoned he... [ಕನ್ನಡ ಆವೃತ್ತಿ / பதிப்பு / संस्करण]
full_text:
A poor fisherman casts net four times. Fourth time he pulls brass jar sealed with Solomon's seal. Opens it, huge Jinni emerges, threatens to kill fisherman because after centuries imprisoned he vowed to kill liberator. Fisherman tricks Jinni by doubting jar could hold him, Jinni re-enters to prove, fisherman seals jar again.

Later Jinni bargains, leads fisherman to lake with colored fish. Fisherman sells fish to king, king discovers city turned to stone, etc. Contains sub-tales of Wazir and Sage Duban, King Sindibad and Falcon, Husband and Parrot, Prince and Ogress.
moral: ನೀತಿ ಪಾಠ: Patience, clear thinking, and humble courage overcome the greatest enchantments.

keywords: the porter and the three ladies of baghdad
full_text:
A porter helps a lady shop, is invited to house of three sisters. They feast, but make him swear not to ask about what they do. Three Kalandars (wandering princes with shaved beards and lost eyes) knock. Ladies admit them with same oath. Then Caliph Harun al-Rashid in disguise with Jafar and banishmenter Masrur knocks, also admitted.

Ladies beat dogs and weep, beat lutes. Porter and guests ask meaning. Ladies explain their histories: first lady was beaten by demon, second lady's tale, portress tale. Kalandars tell their tales. Caliph reveals himself and marries sisters.
moral: ನೀತಿ ಪಾಠ: A wise leader listens to truthful counsel and governs with mercy rather than anger.

full_text:
A tailor's hunchback chokes on fishbone and appears dead. Tailor and wife carry body to doctor's house, doctor trips over body, thinks he defeated, drops body in steward's house, steward thinks thief etc. Body passes to many hands: Christian broker, etc. Each thinks he defeated hunchback.

Finally brought before king, each confesses. Barber called to examine, finds fishbone, removes, hunchback revives. King orders tale recorded. Contains Nazarene Broker's Story, Reeve's Tale, Jewish Doctor, Tailor, Barber's six brothers.

title: The Fox and the Grapes (ಕನ್ನಡ)
summary: A Fox one day spied a beautiful bunch of ripe grapes hanging from a vine trained along the branches of a tree. The grapes seemed ready to burst with juice, and the Fox's mouth watered as he gazed... [ಕನ್ನಡ ಆವೃತ್ತಿ / பதிப்பு / संस्करण]
full_text:
A Fox one day spied a beautiful bunch of ripe grapes hanging from a vine trained along the branches of a tree. The grapes seemed ready to burst with juice, and the Fox's mouth watered as he gazed longingly at them. The bunch hung from a high branch, and the Fox had to jump for it. The first time he jumped he failed to reach it. So he walked a short distance and took a running leap at it, only to fall short once more.

Again and again he tried, but in vain. Now he sat down and looked at the grapes in disgust. 'What a fool I am,' he said. 'Here I am wearing myself out to get a bunch of sour grapes that are not worth gaping for.' And off he went. Moral: It is easy to despise what you cannot get.

title: The Tortoise and the Hare (ಕನ್ನಡ)
summary: A Hare was making fun of the Tortoise one day for being so slow. 'Do you ever get anywhere?' he asked with a mocking laugh. 'Yes,' replied the Tortoise, 'and I get there sooner than you think.... [ಕನ್ನಡ ಆವೃತ್ತಿ / பதிப்பு / संस्करण]
full_text:
A Hare was making fun of the Tortoise one day for being so slow. 'Do you ever get anywhere?' he asked with a mocking laugh. 'Yes,' replied the Tortoise, 'and I get there sooner than you think. I'll run you a race and prove it.' The Hare was much amused at the idea of running a race with the Tortoise, but for the fun of the thing he agreed. So the Fox, who had consented to act as judge, marked the distance and started the runners off.

The Hare was soon far out of sight, and to make the Tortoise feel very deeply how ridiculous it was for him to try a race with a Hare, he lay down beside the course to take a nap until the Tortoise should catch up. The Tortoise meanwhile kept going slowly but steadily, and, after a time, passed the place where the Hare was sleeping. But the Hare slept on very peacefully; and when at last he did wake up, the Tortoise was near the goal. The Hare now ran his swiftest, but he could not overtake the Tortoise in time. Moral: Slow and steady wins the race.

title: The Ant and the Grasshopper (ಕನ್ನಡ)
summary: In a field one summer's day a Grasshopper was hopping about, chirping and singing to its heart's content. An Ant passed by, bearing along with great toil an ear of corn he was taking to the nest.... [ಕನ್ನಡ ಆವೃತ್ತಿ / பதிப்பு / संस्करण]
full_text:
In a field one summer's day a Grasshopper was hopping about, chirping and singing to its heart's content. An Ant passed by, bearing along with great toil an ear of corn he was taking to the nest. 'Why not come and chat with me,' said the Grasshopper, 'instead of toiling and moiling in that way?' 'I am helping to lay up food for the winter,' said the Ant, 'and recommend you to do the same.' 'Why bother about winter?' said the Grasshopper; 'we have got plenty of food at present.' But the Ant went on its way and continued its toil.

When the winter came the Grasshopper had no food and found itself dying of hunger, while it saw the ants distributing every day corn and grain from the stores they had collected in the summer. Then the Grasshopper knew: It is best to prepare for days of need. Moral: Work today for tomorrow.

full_text:
Once when a Lion was asleep a little Mouse began running up and down upon him; this soon wakened the Lion, who placed his huge paw upon him, and opened his big jaws to swallow him. 'Pardon, O King,' cried the little Mouse: 'forgive me this time, I shall never forget it: who knows but what I may be able to do you a turn some of these days?' The Lion was so tickled at the idea of the Mouse being able to help him, that he lifted up his paw and let him go. Some time after the Lion was caught in a trap, and the hunters who desired to carry him alive to the King, tied him to a tree while they went in search of a wagon to carry him on.

Just then the little Mouse happened to pass by, and seeing the sad plight in which the Lion was, went up to him and soon gnawed away the ropes that bound the King of the Beasts. 'Was I not right?' said the little Mouse. Moral: Little friends may prove great friends.

title: The Boy Who Cried Wolf (ಕನ್ನಡ)
summary: There once was a shepherd boy who was bored as he sat on the hillside watching the village sheep. To amuse himself he took a great breath and sang out, 'Wolf! Wolf! The Wolf is chasing the sheep!'... [ಕನ್ನಡ ಆವೃತ್ತಿ / பதிப்பு / संस्करण]
full_text:
There once was a shepherd boy who was bored as he sat on the hillside watching the village sheep. To amuse himself he took a great breath and sang out, 'Wolf! Wolf! The Wolf is chasing the sheep!' The villagers came running up the hill to help the boy drive the wolf away. But when they arrived at the top of the hill, they found no wolf. The boy laughed at the sight of their angry faces. 'Don't cry wolf, shepherd boy,' said the villagers, 'when there's no wolf!' They went grumbling back down the hill. Later, the boy sang out again, 'Wolf! Wolf! The wolf is chasing the sheep!' To his naughty delight, he watched the villagers run up the hill to help him drive the wolf away. When the villagers saw no wolf they sternly said, 'Save your frightened song for when there is really something wrong! Don't cry wolf when there is no wolf!' But the boy just grinned and watched them go grumbling down the hill once more.

Later, he saw a REAL wolf prowling about his flock. Alarmed, he leaped to his feet and sang out as loudly as he could, 'Wolf! Wolf!' But the villagers thought he was trying to fool them again, and so they didn't come. At sunset, the villagers wondered why the shepherd boy hadn't returned with their sheep. They went up the hill to find the boy. They found him weeping. 'There really was a wolf here! The flock has scattered! I cried out, Wolf! Why didn't you come?' An old man tried to comfort the boy as they went to bring back the sheep. 'We'll help you look for the lost sheep in the morning,' he said, putting his arm around the youth, 'Nobody believes a liar...even when he is telling the truth!' Moral: Liars are not believed even when they speak the truth.

title: The Crow and the Pitcher (ಕನ್ನಡ)
summary: A Crow, half-dead with thirst, came upon a Pitcher which had once been full of water; but when the Crow put its beak into the mouth of the Pitcher he found that only a very little water was left... [ಕನ್ನಡ ಆವೃತ್ತಿ / பதிப்பு / संस्करण]
full_text:
A Crow, half-dead with thirst, came upon a Pitcher which had once been full of water; but when the Crow put its beak into the mouth of the Pitcher he found that only a very little water was left in it, and that he could not reach far enough down to get at it. He tried, and he tried, but at last had to give up in despair. Then a thought came to him, and he took a pebble and dropped it into the Pitcher. Then he took another pebble and dropped it into the Pitcher.

Then he took another pebble and dropped that into the Pitcher. Then he took another pebble and dropped that into the Pitcher. At last, at last, he saw the water mount up near him, and after casting in a few more pebbles he was able to quench his thirst and save his life. Moral: Little by little does the trick.

title: The Fox and the Crow (ಕನ್ನಡ)
summary: A Fox once saw a Crow fly off with a piece of cheese in its beak and settle on a branch of a tree. 'That's for me, as I am a Fox,' said Master Reynard, and he walked up to the foot of the tree.... [ಕನ್ನಡ ಆವೃತ್ತಿ / பதிப்பு / संस्करण]
full_text:
A Fox once saw a Crow fly off with a piece of cheese in its beak and settle on a branch of a tree. 'That's for me, as I am a Fox,' said Master Reynard, and he walked up to the foot of the tree. 'Good day, Mistress Crow,' he cried. 'How well you are looking today: how glossy your feathers; how bright your eye.

I feel sure your voice must surpass that of other birds, just as your figure does; let me hear but one song from you that I may greet you as the Queen of Birds.' The Crow lifted up her head and began to caw her best, but the moment she opened her mouth the piece of cheese fell to the ground, only to be snapped up by Master Fox. 'That will do,' said he. 'That was all I wanted. In exchange for your cheese I will give you a piece of advice for the future: Do not trust flatterers.' Moral: Do not trust flatterers.

keywords: the goose that laid the golden eggs
full_text:
There was once a Countryman who possessed the most wonderful Goose you can imagine, for every day when he visited the nest, the Goose had laid a beautiful, glittering, golden egg. The Countryman took the eggs to market and soon began to get rich. But it was not long before he grew impatient with the Goose because she gave him only a single golden egg a day. He was not getting rich fast enough.

Then one day, after he had finished counting his money, the idea came to him that he could get all the golden eggs at once by killing the Goose and cutting it open. But when the deed was done, not a single golden egg did he find, and his precious Goose was dead. Moral: Those who have plenty want more and so lose all they have.

The Wind and the Sun were disputing which was the stronger. Suddenly they saw a traveller coming down the road, and the Sun said: 'I see a way to decide our dispute. Whichever of us can cause that traveller to take off his cloak shall be regarded as the stronger. You begin.' So the Sun retired behind a cloud, and the Wind began to blow as hard as it could upon the traveller.

But the harder he blew the more closely did the traveller wrap his cloak round him, till at last the Wind had to give up in despair. Then the Sun came out and shone in all his glory upon the traveller, who soon found it too hot to walk with his cloak on. Moral: Kindness effects more than severity.

title: Yeh-Shen (Ye Xian) - China - Oldest Known Cinderella (ಕನ್ನಡ)
summary: In ancient China, Chief Wu had two wives. One died leaving daughter Yeh-Shen, beautiful and clever at pottery. Her stepmother hated her and made her work in caves gathering firewood and water.... [ಕನ್ನಡ ಆವೃತ್ತಿ / பதிப்பு / संस्करण]
keywords: yeh-shen (ye xian) - china - oldest known cinderella
full_text:
In ancient China, Chief Wu had two wives. One died leaving daughter Yeh-Shen, beautiful and clever at pottery. Her stepmother hated her and made her work in caves gathering firewood and water. Yeh-Shen had only one friend, a fish with golden eyes in a pond, which she fed daily. Stepmother discovered fish, defeated it and ate it, hiding bones. An old man from heaven told Yeh-Shen to hide fish bones in her room; whatever she wished would be granted. New Year festival came, stepmother forced her to stay home. Yeh-Shen prayed to bones and was given a cloak of kingfisher feathers and tiny golden slippers.

She went to festival, charmed all, but fled losing one slipper when step-siblings chased. A trader from To'han found slipper and presented to king. King searched for owner, trying slipper on all women. Finally Yeh-Shen tried it, it fit perfectly. She wore feather cloak again, king married her. Stepmother and stepsister were banished from the kingdom? Actually they fled and were buried in flying stones in some versions.
moral: ನೀತಿ ಪಾಠ: Wisdom, patience, and kind conduct lead to peace and happiness.

title: Rhodopis - Egypt/Greece - 1st Century BCE (ಕನ್ನಡ)
summary: Rhodopis was a beautiful Greek courtesan living in Naukratis, Egypt. One day while bathing, an eagle (actually Horus?) snatched one of her red-rose gilded slippers and flew away, dropping it in... [ಕನ್ನಡ ಆವೃತ್ತಿ / பதிப்பு / संस्करण]
full_text:
Rhodopis was a beautiful Greek courtesan living in Naukratis, Egypt. One day while bathing, an eagle (actually Horus?) snatched one of her red-rose gilded slippers and flew away, dropping it in lap of Pharaoh Psammetichus in Memphis who was holding court. Pharaoh, struck by small size and beauty of slipper, sent heralds throughout Egypt to find woman to whom slipper belonged.

Prince proclaims he will marry woman who fits glass slipper. Stepsisters try to force foot, fail. Cinderella asks to try, fits, produces second slipper, fairy godmother makes her even more beautiful, marries prince, forgives stepsisters and marries them to lords.

title: Aschenputtel - Germany - Brothers Grimm (ಕನ್ನಡ)
summary: A rich man's wife dies, tells daughter to remain pious. Man remarries woman with two daughters beautiful but evil. They call stepdaughter Aschenputtel (Ashputtel) because she must sit in ashes.... [ಕನ್ನಡ ಆವೃತ್ತಿ / பதிப்பு / संस्करण]
full_text:
A rich man's wife dies, tells daughter to remain pious. Man remarries woman with two daughters beautiful but evil. They call stepdaughter Aschenputtel (Ashputtel) because she must sit in ashes. Father goes to fair, asks what to bring, stepdaughters ask fine clothes, Aschenputtel asks first branch that knocks his hat on way home. Father brings hazel branch, she plants on mother's grave, waters with tears, grows into great tree, white bird lives in it granting wishes. King holds three-day festival to find bride. Aschenputtel asks stepmother to go, denied, stepmother throws lentils into ashes task.

White birds sort lentils. Aschenputtel goes to tree: 'Shiver and quiver little tree, silver and gold throw down over me.' Bird throws gold and silver dress and silk slippers. She goes to ball, prince dances only with her, she escapes. Three nights, dresses more beautiful each night, third night prince spreads pitch, loses gold slipper. Prince goes house to house, stepsisters cut toe and heel to fit, doves cry 'Rook di goo, blood in shoe!' Finally Aschenputtel fits, doves say she is true bride. At wedding, doves peck out stepsisters' eyes for wickedness.
moral: ನೀತಿ ಪಾಠ: Wisdom, patience, and kind conduct lead to peace and happiness.

Woman wants child, witch gives barley seed, grows flower, tiny girl inside Thumbelina. Sleeps in walnut shell. Toad steals to marry to son, fish help escape on lily pad. Cockchafer beetle takes her, finds ugly, leaves.

Field mouse shelters winter, wants her marry mole blind who hates sun. Swallow she saved tells her to flee. Takes her to land of flower prince, Thumbelina becomes queen of flower spirits, gets wings, marries king, renamed Maia.

title: The Little Mermaid (ಕನ್ನಡ)
summary: Far out in the ocean, where the water is as blue as the prettiest cornflower and as clear as crystal, it is very deep. There dwell the Sea King and his subjects. The Sea King's palace is made of... [ಕನ್ನಡ ಆವೃತ್ತಿ / பதிப்பு / संस्करण]
full_text:
Far out in the ocean, where the water is as blue as the prettiest cornflower and as clear as crystal, it is very deep. There dwell the Sea King and his subjects. The Sea King's palace is made of coral. His old mother keeps house, proud of noble birth, with six sea-princesses, youngest the Little Mermaid, with beautiful voice. She is 15, may rise to surface. She sees prince on ship, storm sinks ship, she saves prince, falls in love.

She visits Sea Witch who lives in creepy forest of polyps, gives her voice in exchange for human legs, each step feels like walking on knives. She drinks potion, tail becomes legs, but mute. Prince finds her, loves her as child but loves another princess he thinks saved him. Little Mermaid has chance to kill prince with knife given by sisters who traded hair to witch, to become mermaid again. She cannot, throws knife, throws herself into sea, becomes foam, but becomes daughter of air, earning soul after 300 years of good deeds. Moral on selfless love.

full_text:
An emperor loves fine clothes. Two swindlers claim to be weavers who can make cloth invisible to stupid or unfit. Emperor pays gold. Swindlers pretend weave on empty looms.

Emperor sends old minister who sees nothing but pretends to see to not seem stupid. Emperor himself sees nothing but pretends. He parades naked in supposed clothes. Crowd pretends to admire until child shouts 'But he has nothing on!' Everyone laughs, emperor continues naked parade because cannot admit.

Devil made magic mirror that makes beautiful look ugly. Goblins break it, splinters fly into eyes and hearts making people cold. Kay and Gerda are friends. Splinter enters Kay's eye and heart, he becomes cold, mocks Gerda. Snow Queen, beautiful woman of ice and snow, kisses Kay (two kisses make forget Gerda, third would kill), takes him to palace in Lapland.

Gerda searches: talks to river, old woman who combs hair with magic, crows, robber girl with knife, Lapland woman and Finland woman. Finmark, finds Kay in Snow Queen palace trying to spell 'Eternity' with ice pieces, but cannot. Gerda weeps, tears melt heart, removes splinter, Kay weeps removing eye splinter. They return home, now grown-ups, but children in heart.

full_text:
Far out in the ocean, where the water is as blue as the prettiest cornflower and as clear as crystal, it is very deep. There dwell the Sea King and his subjects. The Sea King's palace is made of coral. His old mother keeps house, proud of noble birth, with six sea-princesses, youngest the Little Mermaid, with beautiful voice. She is 15, may rise to surface. She sees prince on ship, storm sinks ship, she saves prince, falls in love.

She visits Sea Witch who lives in creepy forest of polyps, gives her voice in exchange for human legs, each step feels like walking on knives. She drinks potion, tail becomes legs, but mute. Prince finds her, loves her as child but loves another princess he thinks saved him. Little Mermaid has chance to kill prince with knife given by sisters who traded hair to witch, to become mermaid again. She cannot, throws knife, throws herself into sea, becomes foam, but becomes daughter of air, earning soul after 300 years of good deeds. Moral on selfless love.

full_text:
Far out in the ocean, where the water is as blue as the prettiest cornflower and as clear as crystal, it is very deep. There dwell the Sea King and his subjects. The Sea King's palace is made of coral. His old mother keeps house, proud of noble birth, with six sea-princesses, youngest the Little Mermaid, with beautiful voice. She is 15, may rise to surface. She sees prince on ship, storm sinks ship, she saves prince, falls in love.

She visits Sea Witch who lives in creepy forest of polyps, gives her voice in exchange for human legs, each step feels like walking on knives. She drinks potion, tail becomes legs, but mute. Prince finds her, loves her as child but loves another princess he thinks saved him. Little Mermaid has chance to kill prince with knife given by sisters who traded hair to witch, to become mermaid again. She cannot, throws knife, throws herself into sea, becomes foam, but becomes daughter of air, earning soul after 300 years of good deeds. Moral on selfless love.

Gerda searches: talks to river, old woman who combs hair with magic, crows, robber girl with knife, Lapland woman and Finland woman. Finmark, finds Kay in Snow Queen palace trying to spell 'Eternity' with ice pieces, but cannot. Gerda weeps, tears melt heart, removes splinter, Kay weeps removing eye splinter. full_text:
Far out in the ocean, where the water is as blue as the prettiest cornflower and as clear as crystal, it is very deep. There dwell the Sea King and his subjects. The Sea King's palace is made of coral. His old mother keeps house, proud of noble birth, with six sea-princesses, youngest the Little Mermaid, with beautiful voice. She is 15, may rise to surface. She sees prince on ship, storm sinks ship, she saves prince, falls in love.

She visits Sea Witch who lives in creepy forest of polyps, gives her voice in exchange for human legs, each step feels like walking on knives. She drinks potion, tail becomes legs, but mute. Prince finds her, loves her as child but loves another princess he thinks saved him. Little Mermaid has chance to kill prince with knife given by sisters who traded hair to witch, to become mermaid again. She cannot, throws knife, throws herself into sea, becomes foam, but becomes daughter of air, earning soul after 300 years of good deeds. Moral on selfless love.

title: Vessantara Jataka - The Prince Who Gave Everything (ಕನ್ನಡ)
summary: Vessantara, last birth before Buddha, was prince renowned for generosity. He had magic elephant that brings rain, gave it to enemy kingdom suffering drought. People angry, king Vessantara's father... [ಕನ್ನಡ ಆವೃತ್ತಿ / பதிப்பு / संस्करण]
keywords: vessantara jataka - the prince who gave everything
full_text:
Vessantara, last birth before Buddha, was prince renowned for generosity. He had magic elephant that brings rain, gave it to enemy kingdom suffering drought. People angry, king Vessantara's father banishes him. Vessantara leaves with wife Maddi and two children Jali and Kanhajina. On way gives away carriage, horses. Lives in Vamka mountain hermitage. Brahmin Jujaka, cruel old man, asks for children as servants.

Vessantara gives children, though heart breaks, as ultimate Dana Paramita perfection of generosity. Sakka as the king of clouds tests him asking for wife Maddi, he gives. Sakka returns wife. Jujaka brings children to city, grandfather King Sanjaya ransoms grandchildren, Jujaka dies overeating. Vessantara returns as king. This Jataka taught for centuries, illustrates perfect charity. Moral: Supreme generosity leads to Buddhahood.
moral: ನೀತಿ ಪಾಠ: Paramita perfection - Dana, Sila, Kshanti etc.

summary: King Sibi (Sivi) famous for self-sacrifice. the king of clouds as hawk and Agni as dove test him. Dove flies to Sibi's lap seeking refuge from hawk. Hawk says 'Dove is my food, give me.' Sibi says 'I must... [ಕನ್ನಡ ಆವೃತ್ತಿ / பதிப்பு / संस्करण]
keywords: sibi jataka - king sibi and dove
full_text:
King Sibi (Sivi) famous for self-sacrifice. the king of clouds as hawk and Agni as dove test him. Dove flies to Sibi's lap seeking refuge from hawk. Hawk says 'Dove is my food, give me.' Sibi says 'I must protect refugee.' Hawk: 'Then give equal weight of your flesh.' Sibi cuts flesh from thigh, puts on scale, dove always heavier.

Finally Sibi himself sits on scale giving whole body. Gods reveal themselves, heal him, bless. Moral: King protects even small creature at cost of self.

title: Chaddanta Jataka - Six-Tusked Elephant (ಕನ್ನಡ)
summary: Bodhisatta born as Chaddanta, chief of 8000 elephants, six-tusked white elephant, with two wives Mahasubhadda and Cullasubhadda. Cullasubhadda jealous of Mahasubhadda. She prays to be queen in... [ಕನ್ನಡ ಆವೃತ್ತಿ / பதிப்பு / संस्करण]
full_text:
Bodhisatta born as Chaddanta, chief of 8000 elephants, six-tusked white elephant, with two wives Mahasubhadda and Cullasubhadda. Cullasubhadda jealous of Mahasubhadda. She prays to be queen in next life to kill Chaddanta. Reborn as queen of Benares, feigns illness, says only six-tusked elephant tusks will cure. King sends hunter Sonuttara, who after 7 years finds Chaddanta.

Chaddanta, seeing hunter tired, feeds him. Hunter shoots Chaddanta with poison arrow. Chaddanta, though dying, helps hunter cut tusks, not angry, forgives queen. Queen sees tusks, realizes his forgiveness, dies of remorse. Moral: Forgiveness even to murderer - Kshanti Paramita.
moral: ನೀತಿ ಪಾಠ: Paramita perfection - Dana, Sila, Kshanti etc.

title: Nigrodha Jataka - Banyan Deer (ಕನ್ನಡ)
summary: Bodhisatta born as Banyan Deer King, golden deer with herd of 500, rival herd Sakha with 500. King of Benares hunts daily. Deer kings agree to send one deer daily by lot to king's kitchen to avoid... [ಕನ್ನಡ ಆವೃತ್ತಿ / பதிப்பு / संस्करण]
full_text:
Bodhisatta born as Banyan Deer King, golden deer with herd of 500, rival herd Sakha with 500. King of Benares hunts daily. Deer kings agree to send one deer daily by lot to king's kitchen to avoid whole herd slaughter. One day lot falls on pregnant doe in Sakha's herd, she begs Sakha, Sakha refuses, she goes to Bodhisatta Banyan deer. Bodhisatta says 'Go, I will go in your place.' Bodhisatta goes to banishment block.

Cook sees golden deer, reports king. King asks why. Banyan deer speaks: 'I came for doe.' King moved by sacrifice, spares all deer, grants abhaya dana - safety to all animals. Moral: Compassionate king self-sacrifice.
moral: ನೀತಿ ಪಾಠ: Paramita perfection - Dana, Sila, Kshanti etc.

title: Vessantara - Last of Ten Great Jatakas (ಕನ್ನಡ)
summary: Vessantara, last birth before Buddha, was prince renowned for generosity. He had magic elephant that brings rain, gave it to enemy kingdom suffering drought. People angry, king Vessantara's father... [ಕನ್ನಡ ಆವೃತ್ತಿ / பதிப்பு / संस्करण]
keywords: vessantara - last of ten great jatakas
full_text:
Vessantara, last birth before Buddha, was prince renowned for generosity. He had magic elephant that brings rain, gave it to enemy kingdom suffering drought. People angry, king Vessantara's father banishes him. Vessantara leaves with wife Maddi and two children Jali and Kanhajina. On way gives away carriage, horses. Lives in Vamka mountain hermitage. Brahmin Jujaka, cruel old man, asks for children as servants.

Vessantara gives children, though heart breaks, as ultimate Dana Paramita perfection of generosity. Sakka as the king of clouds tests him asking for wife Maddi, he gives. Sakka returns wife. Jujaka brings children to city, grandfather King Sanjaya ransoms grandchildren, Jujaka dies overeating. Vessantara returns as king. This Jataka taught for centuries, illustrates perfect charity. Moral: Supreme generosity leads to Buddhahood.

keywords: sivi jataka - king sivi gives eyes
full_text:
King Sibi (Sivi) famous for self-sacrifice. the king of clouds as hawk and Agni as dove test him. Dove flies to Sibi's lap seeking refuge from hawk. Hawk says 'Dove is my food, give me.' Sibi says 'I must protect refugee.' Hawk: 'Then give equal weight of your flesh.' Sibi cuts flesh from thigh, puts on scale, dove always heavier.

Finally Sibi himself sits on scale giving whole body. Gods reveal themselves, heal him, bless. Moral: King protects even small creature at cost of self.
moral: ನೀತಿ ಪಾಠ: Paramita perfection - Dana, Sila, Kshanti etc.

title: Sasa Jataka - The Hare and Moon (ಕನ್ನಡ)
summary: Once Bodhisatta was born as a hare. He lived with monkey, jackal, otter. They decided to keep Uposatha fast. A Brahmin (Sakka in disguise) came begging food. Monkey gave mangoes, otter fish,... [ಕನ್ನಡ ಆವೃತ್ತಿ / பதிப்பு / संस्करण]
keywords: sasa jataka - the hare and moon
full_text:
Once Bodhisatta was born as a hare. He lived with monkey, jackal, otter. They decided to keep Uposatha fast. A Brahmin (Sakka in disguise) came begging food. Monkey gave mangoes, otter fish, jackal stolen meat, but hare had only grass which Brahmin cannot eat.

So hare said 'Use me as food' and jumped into fire. Sakka revealed himself, did not let hare burn, took hare and painted his image on moon for all to see. Hence moon has hare. Moral: Perfect self-sacrifice Dana Paramita.
moral: ನೀತಿ ಪಾಠ: Paramita perfection - Dana, Sila, Kshanti etc.

title: La Belle au bois dormant - Sleeping Beauty in the Wood (ಕನ್ನಡ)
summary: There once was a king and queen who longed for child, at last queen bore daughter. Christening, invited seven fairies as godmothers giving gifts: beauty, wit, grace, dance, song etc. Old fairy not... [ಕನ್ನಡ ಆವೃತ್ತಿ / பதிப்பு / संस्करण]
keywords: la belle au bois dormant - sleeping beauty in the wood
full_text:
There once was a king and queen who longed for child, at last queen bore daughter. Christening, invited seven fairies as godmothers giving gifts: beauty, wit, grace, dance, song etc. Old fairy not invited for 50 years in tower thought dead, appears angry, curses: princess shall pierce hand with spindle and die. Youngest fairy mitigates: not die but sleep 100 years until prince awakens. King bans spindles. At 15 or 16, princess wandering castle finds old woman spinning, pricks finger, falls asleep, fairy puts all castle to sleep, forest of thorns grows.

After 100 years, prince from another kingdom hunts, hears tale, cuts through thorns (they open for him). Finds princess sleeping beautiful, kneels, she awakens, whole castle awakens. Prince marries. But prince's mother is ogress who wants to eat children? In Perrault's extended version, they have two children Dawn (Aurore) and Day (Jour), ogress mother-in-law tries to have steward cook them with Sauce Robert, steward substitutes animals, finally ogress tries to throw queen and children into vat of vipers, but king returns and ogress throws herself in. Moral: No woman waits so long for husband without trouble but tale says marriage still happy.
moral: ನೀತಿ ಪಾಠ: Virtue and patience rewarded, but second part warns of cruel in-laws

title: Le Petit Chaperon rouge - Little Red Riding Hood (ಕನ್ನಡ)
summary: There was once a little village girl, prettiest ever seen, mother and grandmother doted, grandmother made red hood (chaperon), called Little Red Riding Hood. Mother sends her with cake and pot of... [ಕನ್ನಡ ಆವೃತ್ತಿ / பதிப்பு / संस्करण]
keywords: le petit chaperon rouge - little red riding hood
full_text:
There was once a little village girl, prettiest ever seen, mother and grandmother doted, grandmother made red hood (chaperon), called Little Red Riding Hood. Mother sends her with cake and pot of butter to grandmother sick in other village. Girl goes through wood, meets wolf who wants to eat her but fears woodcutters nearby. Wolf asks where going, girl tells. Wolf says I go this way you that way, see who arrives first. Wolf runs short way, arrives, kills grandmother, eats her (in some versions), puts her clothes, lies in bed.

Little Red Riding Hood knocks, wolf disguises voice. Girl enters: 'Grandmother what big arms you have!' 'All the better to hug you.' 'What big legs!' 'All the better to run.' 'What big ears!' 'All the better to hear.' 'What big eyes!' 'All the better to see.' 'What big teeth!' 'All the better to eat you!' And wolf eats her. Perrault ends here with moral warning, no rescue. In later Grimm version huntsman saves. Moral: Young girls should not listen to strangers, especially charming wolves.
moral: ನೀತಿ ಪಾಠ: Don't trust strangers - especially smooth-talking wolves

title: La Barbe bleue - Blue Beard (ಕನ್ನಡ)
summary: There was a man with fine houses and blue beard which made him ugly and frightening, wives disappeared mysteriously. He courts neighboring gentleman's two daughters, younger eventually marries for... [ಕನ್ನಡ ಆವೃತ್ತಿ / பதிப்பு / संस्करण]
full_text:
There was a man with fine houses and blue beard which made him ugly and frightening, wives disappeared mysteriously. He courts neighboring gentleman's two daughters, younger eventually marries for wealth despite fear. Month after wedding he says must travel, gives keys to wife: all rooms open except small closet at end of gallery, forbids to enter or else wrath. She promises. He leaves. She invites sister Anne and friends, they tour palace, but curiosity overcomes, she opens closet: floor covered in blood, dead bodies of previous wives hung on wall (throats cut).

She drops key in blood, blood won't wash off (magic key). Blue Beard returns early, sees blood on key, says you shall join them tonight. She begs time to pray, calls sister Anne on tower to watch for brothers. 'Anne, sister Anne, do you see anyone coming?' 'I see only sun and grass.' Brothers - dragoon and musketeer - arrive, kill Blue Beard, wife inherits fortune, marries worthy man. Moral: Curiosity is dangerous but disobedience in marriage? Perrault gives two morals.
moral: ನೀತಿ ಪಾಠ: Curiosity defeated wives, but also tale of female curiosity and male tyranny

summary: Miller dies leaving to three sons: mill to eldest, donkey to second, cat to youngest. Youngest despairs. Cat says 'Give me bag and boots, trust me.' Cat puts boots, goes to warren, puts bran and... [ಕನ್ನಡ ಆವೃತ್ತಿ / பதிப்பு / संस्करण]
keywords: le maître chat ou le chat botté - puss in boots / master cat
full_text:
Miller dies leaving to three sons: mill to eldest, donkey to second, cat to youngest. Youngest despairs. Cat says 'Give me bag and boots, trust me.' Cat puts boots, goes to warren, puts bran and sow-thistle in bag, catches rabbit, presents to king as gift from Marquis of Carabas (his master). Does same with partridges. Months. One day king drives with daughter princess by river. Cat tells master undress and bathe in river, hides clothes. When king passes cat shouts 'Help!

Marquis of Carabas drowning!' King sends clothes, welcomes. Cat runs ahead, tells peasants mowing and reaping to tell king fields belong to Marquis of Carabas or will be minced. Comes to castle of ogre who can transform to any animal. Cat asks to see: ogre becomes lion, cat pretends fear then asks to become mouse, ogre becomes mouse, cat eats him. Castle now his master's. King arrives, sees castle, thinks Marquis rich, Marquis marries princess. Cat becomes great lord who hunts only for amusement. Moral: Industry and know-how worth more than inherited wealth.
moral: ನೀತಿ ಪಾಠ: Cleverness and audacity can make fortune

Father in wife's power. Prince gives ball two nights. Stepsisters go fine, Cinderella weeps, fairy godmother appears, asks for pumpkin, mice, rat, lizards. Pumpkin to coach, mice to horses, rat to coachman, lizards to footmen, rags to cloth of gold and silver with glass slippers. Warns leave before midnight.

Cinderella goes, prince admires, she leaves before midnight first night. Second night stays till midnight, clock strikes twelve, loses glass slipper fleeing. Prince proclaims he will marry who fits slipper. Stepsisters try force foot, fail. Cinderella asks to try, fits, produces second slipper, fairy makes her more beautiful, prince marries, Cinderella forgives stepsisters, lodges them in palace and marries them to two great lords. full_text:
Woodcutter and wife have seven sons, youngest tiny at birth no bigger than thumb, called Little Thumbling (Petit Poucet), but very clever, though thought dull because he listened. Family poor, parents decide to abandon children in forest to not starve. Thumbling overhears, puts white pebbles in pocket, drops to find way back. Parents take them again, this time Thumbling has only bread crumbs, birds eat. Lost in forest, they find ogre's house. Ogre's wife hides them, ogre comes sniffing fresh meat, wants to eat boys, wife says tomorrow. Ogre has seven daughters who are also ogresses.

At night Thumbling swaps his brothers' crowns with ogress daughters' crowns (or caps), ogre in dark cuts daughters' throats instead. They flee. Ogre puts seven-league boots and chases. Thumbling steals boots while ogre sleeps exhausted on rock. With boots he runs to ogre's house, tells wife ogre captured by robbers demands ransom, takes all money, returns to parents rich, buys offices for brothers, becomes king's messenger with boots. Moral: Little cleverness beats brute strength.
moral: ನೀತಿ ಪಾಠ: Cleverness of smallest can save family

title: Griselidis - Griselda (verse tale) (ಕನ್ನಡ)
summary: Prince loves virtuous shepherdess Griselidis, marries her despite courtiers. To test her patience and virtue, he takes away her daughter saying will kill, then son, then says will repudiate her to... [ಕನ್ನಡ ಆವೃತ್ತಿ / பதிப்பு / संस्करण]
full_text:

title: Peau d'Ane - Donkey Skin (ಕನ್ನಡ)
summary: Great king with beautiful queen dying makes promise not marry except woman more beautiful than her. Queen dies. King looks, only daughter more beautiful than mother. King, blinded, wants to marry... [ಕನ್ನಡ ಆವೃತ್ತಿ / பதிப்பு / संस्करण]
full_text:
Great king with beautiful queen dying makes promise not marry except woman more beautiful than her. Queen dies. King looks, only daughter more beautiful than mother. King, blinded, wants to marry daughter (incest motif). Daughter, advised by fairy godmother Lilac (Fée des Lilas), asks impossible gifts to delay: dress color of sky, color of moon, color of sun, then skin of donkey that excretes gold (king's wealth source). King grants all. Daughter flees wearing donkey skin disguise, Peau d'Ane, works as pig keeper in farm. Prince visits farm, sees her beautiful despite donkey skin through keyhole, falls in love.

He asks for cake made by Donkey Skin. She puts ring in cake. Prince chokes? Finds ring, says will marry woman whom ring fits. All try, Donkey Skin's tiny hand fits, she drops donkey skin revealing dress color of sun, marries prince. Donkey skin version of Catskin 510B. Moral: Virtue triumphs over desperate father.
moral: ನೀತಿ ಪಾಠ: Virtue and modesty survive even in donkey skin

keywords: vetala story 1: the prince who married four wives
full_text:
King Vikramaditya (Vikram) of Ujjain must bring Vetala (Betal) a mysterious riddle-teller Vetal in ancient forest to yogi. Vetala tells story and asks riddle, if Vikram answers, Vetala flies back, if not speaks, head bursts. Vikram's wisdom makes him answer, cycle repeats 25 times. On 25th, Vikram stays silent, brings Vetala, yogi tries to kill Vikram but Vetala warns and Vikram kills yogi, gains boon.

title: The Loss of Friends (Frame) (ಕನ್ನಡ)
summary: In the city of Mahilaropya there was a king named Amarashakti who had three dull-witted sons. He sought a teacher who could make them wise in niti. An old Brahmin named the great preserver Sharma promised to... [ಕನ್ನಡ ಆವೃತ್ತಿ / பதிப்பு / संस्करण]
full_text:
In the city of Mahilaropya there was a king named Amarashakti who had three dull-witted sons. He sought a teacher who could make them wise in niti. An old Brahmin named the great preserver Sharma promised to do it in six months through stories. He began: There was a city called Mahilaropya, merchants, and a lion king in the forest named Pingalaka who ruled. His ministers were two jackals, Karataka and Damanaka, sons of a former minister, now unemployed. One day, a merchant's bull named Sanjivaka was left in the forest and became friends with Pingalaka, making the lion neglect his kingdom.

Damanaka grew jealous and decided to break their friendship. He sowed distrust by telling the lion the bull plotted to kill him, and telling the bull the lion would kill him. The lion and bull fought and the bull died. The jackals regained power. But the great preserver Sharma then says: This is the loss of friends caused by wicked counsel. And to explain how it happens, Damanaka tells stories, and others reply.
moral: ನೀತಿ ಪಾಠ: Loyal friendship and mutual trust overcome the greatest hardships.

title: The Wedge-Pulling Monkey (ಕನ್ನಡ)
summary: A merchant was building a temple near his town. The carpenters working there went to eat, leaving a log half-split with a wedge in it. A troop of monkeys came playing. One foolish monkey, whose... [ಕನ್ನಡ ಆವೃತ್ತಿ / பதிப்பு / संस्करण]
full_text:
A merchant was building a temple near his town. The carpenters working there went to eat, leaving a log half-split with a wedge in it. A troop of monkeys came playing. One foolish monkey, whose death was near, sat on the log and began pulling at the wedge, saying 'What is this in the wrong place?' His tail and paws were caught in the cleft.

When he pulled the wedge out, the log closed and he was trapped until the carpenters returned. Moral: The fool who meddles in what he does not understand comes to grief. This is what happens when you interfere in others' work.
moral: ನೀತಿ ಪಾಠ: Wisdom, patience, and kind conduct lead to peace and happiness.

title: The Jackal and the War-Drum (ಕನ್ನಡ)
summary: A starving jackal named Gomaya wandered into a battlefield and found nothing but a war-drum left behind. The wind blew and a creeper struck the drum: 'Boom!' The jackal was terrified, then... [ಕನ್ನಡ ಆವೃತ್ತಿ / பதிப்பு / संस्करण]
full_text:
A starving jackal named Gomaya wandered into a battlefield and found nothing but a war-drum left behind. The wind blew and a creeper struck the drum: 'Boom!' The jackal was terrified, then thought: what makes this sound must be full of food. He crept closer and found only wood and skin.

He tore it open and found it empty. He said to himself: I thought this big noise had much inside, but it is nothing. So a loud boaster may be empty inside.

summary: Credulous fiend: A Brahmin found a fiend (demon) who served him, demon said he must be kept busy or will eat him. Brahmin gave tasks, demon finished quickly, Brahmin tricked demon with hairy?... [ಕನ್ನಡ ಆವೃತ್ತಿ / பதிப்பு / संस्करण]
full_text:
Credulous fiend: A Brahmin found a fiend (demon) who served him, demon said he must be kept busy or will eat him. Brahmin gave tasks, demon finished quickly, Brahmin tricked demon with hairy?

Actually story: Demon asked work, Brahmin gave impossible task of making rope from ashes, demon stuck. Or fiend who washed feet?
moral: ನೀತಿ ಪಾಠ: Wisdom, patience, and kind conduct lead to peace and happiness.
